newsitem.title: USA: IMM currencies end mixed, some contracts firm late.
newsitem.headline: IMM currencies end mixed, some contracts firm late.

text.p: IMM currency futures closed mixed, with March yen climbing to session highs late in the day after an Asian central bank pulled its bid for dollar/yen, floor traders said.
According to one floor trader, the bank placed a bid for dollar/yen at 121.80, or $0.008233 in March, in late trade.
"They pulled it and then March yen shot up to $0.008252," he said.
One firm, which had been an active player in the IMM currency pits all day, bought 500 March yen contracts at the $0.008250 level.

Some traders said the technical failure of the dollar/mark to re-test the 1.6800 spot mark also boosted mark and Swiss franc futures off their lows near the end of a lightly traded session. March marks held above the 1.68-spot equivalent of $0.5960, and firmed in the final minutes of pit trade to $0.5990.
Another floor source noted that one firm was an active buyer of mark futures, spreading the contracts against Swiss franc futures.
Earlier in the session, one local firm bought 1,000 March sterling against 1,000 March marks.
One floor trader said activity in Mexican peso futures turned active after news that a Mexican state governor warned that the peso was overvalued and headed for a new meltdown.
Vicente Fox, governor of the central state of Guanajuato and a leading opposition figure, took full-page ads in local newspapers warning that the peso was 2.4 percent overvalued.
"Some people think Fox's comments were politically motivated more than anything," the trader said.
However, March pesos, which traded as high as $0.128050 during the day, fell to $0.127750.

Traders said the key IMM currency futures were likely to trade within ranges overnight ahead of U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on Wednesday. The second leg of his semiannual testimony on U.S. monetary policy was rescheduled to Wednesday, March 5.
"Nobody is going to take the dollar higher ahead of Greenspan," one trader said.

At the end of pit trade, March yen was up $0.000038 at $0.008249, marks were up $0.0001 at $0.5986, Swiss francs were down $0.0018 at $0.6856, sterling was $0.0012 higher at $1.6354, Canadian dollars were up $0.0011 at $0.7359, and Australian dollars were down $0.0017 at $0.7765.
